title: Daily arXiv Physics — Friday, 30 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This ordering is inferred from SciRate's community-curated feed, outside discussion, and concrete cross-subfield results. Citation evidence is limited for papers announced only days ago, so this is a notable-paper roundup rather than a measured popularity list. Sunday 1 November had no newer regular batch; this uses the prior Friday batch.

sections.title: Shor's algorithm compiled on cat qubits: 22 593 qubits for RSA-2048 in 3.14 days
sections.abstract: The authors compile Shor's algorithm into superconducting cat-qubit architectures and estimate resources for RSA-2048 and discrete-log benchmarks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It leads SciRate's current Top arXiv papers feed, a checkable community-attention signal; the paper also provides an unusually complete physical-level circuit, layout, and schedule estimate.
sections.claimed_result: The authors estimate 22,593 cat qubits and 3.14 days for a full RSA-2048 compilation, assuming a 1 μs error-correction cycle, 10 μs decoder reaction, phase-flip probability 5×10⁻⁴, and no bit flips during the computation. Their less complete ECDLP/FFDLP estimates reuse compiled operations.
sections.evidence_type: computational; end-to-end circuit compilation, physical-qubit layout, scheduling, and resource estimation—not a hardware demonstration
sections.unique_caveat: The headline estimate depends on an idealized no-bit-flip assumption equivalent to roughly a 100-year bit-flip time. The authors estimate about 45,000 cat qubits if a one-hour bit-flip time is protected by an added code layer; the other cryptographic instances are less completely compiled.

sections.title: High-Fidelity Universal Quantum Gates in a Cryogenic Atom Array
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate a universal gate set in a cryogenic cesium atom array, reporting 99.970(2)% single-qubit fidelity and 99.76(8)% raw two-qubit entangling-gate fidelity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Surfaced in SciRate's current Top arXiv feed and separately discussed by Quantum Crier and the Quantum Research Center. Its atomic-physics/quantum-information cross-list and quantified gate benchmark are concrete signals; the coverage is not independent experimental replication.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measure 99.970(2)% single-qubit Clifford fidelity and 99.76(8)% raw CZ fidelity in a cryogenic ¹³³Cs array, using direct single-photon excitation to a Rydberg P state. Their error model attributes the remaining dominant infidelity to atomic motion, with Rydberg-decay error below 3×10⁻⁴.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; randomized and stabilizer benchmarking in a 4 K optical-tweezer atom array
sections.unique_caveat: These are physical-gate results, not logical or fault-tolerant computation. Atomic motion currently dominates; the higher fidelity projected with improved cooling and other upgrades is a model prediction, not the measured result.

sections.title: Experimental Observation of Error-Resilience Phase Transition on Superconducting Quantum Processor
sections.abstract: The authors test a predicted error-resilience transition on a superconducting processor, using fidelity, Rényi-2 entanglement, and stabilizer Rényi-2 entropy for circuits up to 26 qubits.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Appears in SciRate's current Top arXiv feed and reports a hardware study of a theoretically predicted transition using three observables, alongside noiseless simulations of the same circuit family.
sections.claimed_result: On IBM's ibm_pittsburgh Heron r3, the authors infer a finite-size critical noise angle near 1.01; noiseless simulation of their implemented circuit ensemble gives about 1.05, while the Haar-random model predicts about 1.14. They attribute the shift to circuits too shallow to be truly Haar-random.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; IBM superconducting processor, randomized measurements, zero-noise extrapolation, M3 readout mitigation, and Gaussian-process finite-size analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The transition is identified only after error mitigation and finite-size modelling; raw unmitigated data do not support the fit. The observed critical angle is not the thermodynamic Haar-random value.

sections.title: Individually Addressed Logical Pauli Measurements by QLDPC Surgery on a Trapped Ion Quantum Computer
sections.abstract: The authors implement QLDPC surgery on a trapped-ion processor to measure selected logical Pauli operators while preserving a spectator logical qubit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Surfaced in SciRate's current Top arXiv feed; it is a direct hardware test of a logical-operation primitive needed by low-overhead QLDPC architectures, with reported error intervals.
sections.claimed_result: On Quantinuum's H2-2, a single-round measurement of X̄₁ on a [[10,2,3]] generalized bicycle code has a reported 0.72% error (95% credible interval 0.32–1.41%); three-round decoding reduces the gadget-measurement error below 0.26%. The authors also demonstrate sequential X̄₁ and Z̄₂ measurements while reusing gadget qubits.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; trapped-ion processor, QLDPC surgery gadgets, and three rounds of syndrome extraction
sections.unique_caveat: This validates a primitive on a small, distance-3 code; it does not establish scalable or fault-tolerant operation at larger code distance.

sections.title: Dark-field Search for Quantum Vacuum Signals in the Low-Energy Regime
sections.abstract: The authors describe a European XFEL/ReLaX dark-field search that sees no excess light-by-light scattering and derives a 95% upper bound at 116 eV.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete rare-signal search at the European XFEL combines a high-energy-physics/optics cross-list with a quantified limit from 2,751 pump–probe collisions. This is a notable experimental constraint, not a detection.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report no excess above background and derive a 95% confidence upper limit on the low-energy light-by-light cross section of 7×10⁴ times the QED prediction. The paper details the apparatus and analysis; it identifies the result as also reported in a companion Letter.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; European XFEL HED instrument, the 300-TW ReLaX laser, polarization filtering, and start-to-end simulations at a 116 eV center-of-mass photon energy
sections.unique_caveat: This first implementation is background-limited, with sensitivity constrained by beamline geometry, laser performance, and imperfect correlation between diagnostics and detector counts; the bound is not evidence of a quantum-vacuum signal.

sections.title: Measurements of transverse kinematic imbalance in muon neutrino charged-current interactions on argon with a single proton and no pions in the final state with SBND
sections.abstract: The SBND collaboration reports its first neutrino–argon differential cross sections for muon-neutrino events with one proton and no pions, using 12,804 selected candidates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The first SBND cross-section measurement uses a substantial Run 1 sample and provides a checkable comparison of neutrino event-generator predictions; this is a notable facility result rather than a popularity signal.
sections.claimed_result: From 8.8×10¹⁹ protons-on-target, the authors select 12,804 signal candidates at 91% purity and extract flux-averaged cross sections versus three transverse-kinematic-imbalance variables. None of the compared generators describes all three, with the largest mismatch in transverse missing momentum.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; SBND liquid-argon detector at Fermilab, Run 1 data, flux prediction, detector-response simulation, and unfolded cross-section analysis
sections.unique_caveat: Flux, interaction modelling, secondary interactions, detector response, and unfolding contribute systematic/model dependence; the disagreement is with tested generator predictions, not a model-independent discovery.

sections.title: Scale-free wave localization at topological multicriticality
sections.abstract: The authors combine catastrophe-theory analysis with acoustic metamaterial experiments to show a topological boundary mode with linear, rather than exponential, spatial decay at tricriticality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The optics/condensed-matter cross-list connects a mathematical bulk–boundary result to a directly measured real-space signature in a tunable acoustic metamaterial; included for scientific reach, not a measured attention score.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that an n-th-order topological multicritical point can enforce a boundary-mode envelope proportional to the (n−1)th power of distance, and experimentally demonstrate linear decay in a one-dimensional acoustic platform at a tricritical point. They also generalize the construction to two-dimensional corner modes.
sections.evidence_type: experimental and theoretical; acoustic metamaterial measurements in 1D plus singularity-theory and spatial-transfer-matrix analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The reported experimental demonstration is one-dimensional and requires tricritical tuning; the two-dimensional result is presented as a generalization, not as an independent experimental confirmation in this report.
